Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a diffuse reticulonodular pattern involving both lungs and blunting of the costophrenic angles consistent with bilateral pleural effusions. This combination of diffuse interstitial markings and bilateral fluid is most characteristic of an interstitial lung disease (such as lymphangitic carcinomatosis or sarcoidosis) among the provided choices, whereas heart failure typically presents with cardiomegaly and LCH with upper lobe cysts/nodules sparing the bases.
